source_text:
Ἐπειδὴ κατὰ τὴν προσευχὴν ὑμῶν καὶ κατὰ τὰ σπλάγχνα, ἃ ἔχετε ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, ἀπηγγέλη μοι εἰρηνεύειν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τὴν ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ τῆς Συρίας, πρέπον ἐστὶν ὑμῖν ὡς ἐκκλησίᾳ θεοῦ, χειροτονῆσαι διάκονον εἰς τὸ πρεσβεῦσαι ἐκεῖ θεοῦ πρεσβείαν, εἰς τὸ συγχαρῆναι αὐτοῖς ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ γενομένοις καὶ δοξάσαι τὸ ὄνομα.
μακάριος ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ, ὃς καταξιωθήσεται τῆς τοιαύτης διακονίας, καὶ ὑμεῖς δοξασθήσεσθε. θέλουσιν δὲ ὑμῖν οὐκ ἔστιν ἀδύνατον ὑπὲρ ὀνόματος θεοῦ, ὡς καὶ αἱ ἔγγιστα ἐκκλησίαι ἔπεμψαν ἐπισκόπους, αἱ δὲ πρεσβυτέρους καὶ διακόνους.
thought_title: Send a deacon to Antioch to rejoice with the church at peace
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Smyrna, urging them to send a representative to the church in Antioch, which is now at peace.
pass_a_gloss: Since according to the prayer of you and according to the inward parts which you have in Christ Jesus, it was announced to me [that] to be at peace [is] the church the [one] in Antioch of Syria, it is fitting for you as [a] church of God, to appoint [a] deacon for the [purpose] to go as messenger there [with] God's embassy, for the [purpose] to rejoice together with them [who] to the same [place] came and to glorify the name. Blessed in Jesus Christ [is he] who will be deemed worthy of such service, and you will be glorified. [If] you wish, not is impossible for you on behalf of [the] name of God, as also the nearest churches sent bishops, and [others] elders and deacons.

choices.why: The Greek word means inward parts or bowels, used metaphorically for deep affection; 'compassion' conveys the emotional sense in natural English while 'inward parts' is kept in the literal gloss.

choices.english: to go there as God's ambassador
choices.why: The cognate verb and noun form an idiom for serving as an envoy; rendering the noun as 'embassy' in the literal gloss and the whole phrase as 'God's ambassador' in the natural gloss preserves the sense.
rejected: to perform an embassy of God there
to go there on God's embassy

choices.why: The phrase 'to the same place' is an idiom for gathering together; the natural gloss uses the idiomatic English while the literal gloss keeps the source wording.
rejected: having come to the same place

choices.term: θέλουσιν δὲ ὑμῖν οὐκ ἔστιν ἀδύνατον
choices.english: If you want to do this, it is not impossible for you
choices.why: The dative participle 'θέλουσιν' is conditional in force; the natural gloss makes the condition explicit and supplies the implied object.
rejected: for you who wish, it is not impossible
to those who wish among you, it is not impossible

choices.english: for the sake of God's name
choices.why: The preposition 'ὑπέρ' with the genitive here means 'for the sake of'; the phrase explains the motive for the action.
rejected: on behalf of the name of God

pass_b_english: I have received word that the church in Antioch of Syria is at peace, because of your prayers and the compassion you have in Christ Jesus. It is fitting for you, as a church of God, to appoint a deacon to go there as God's envoy, so that he may rejoice with them when they have gathered together and glorify the name.

Blessed in Jesus Christ is the one who will be deemed worthy of such a ministry, and you will be glorified. If you want to do this, it is not impossible for you for the sake of God's name, just as the nearest churches sent bishops, and others sent elders and deacons.

problems.why: Same office rendered two ways; readers may miss the equivalence.
problems.fix: Use 'council of elders (presbyters)' at first occurrence.

problems.why: 'Ambassador' may be too diplomatic; likely means 'messenger' or 'delegate.'
problems.fix: Use 'messenger of God' or 'delegate for God.'

fixed: The glossary issue about 'council of elders' is not present in this passage; the English uses 'elders' which is consistent with the source's πρεσβυτέρους. No change needed here.
Changed 'ambassador' to 'messenger' in both the English and the literal gloss to better reflect the source's πρεσβεῦσαι.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening sentence by separating the report of peace from the instruction, named the deacon as God's envoy rather than messenger, and smoothed the final sentence so the comparison to other churches reads naturally.

notes.why: 'Messenger' (angelos) could mean 'angel' or 'messenger'; context requires human delegate.
notes.fix: 'Messenger' with note that Greek angelos means both.
